I planted a Blue Wave lacecap hydrangea last month and it isn't doing as well as the other hydrangea I planted at the same time; what is wrong with it, how can I help?

What zone are you in? And does it have the same sun exposure as the others, and was it the same size/growing stage as the others when planted?

Hydrangeas are water pigs and if the dry out too much, the leaves might crisp up a bit. Also, they should have around 6 hours of sun a day (more for blooming than leaves), but if you are in a warm climate, they need a bit of protection from overheating. That might cause the brown leaves.

Root rot is possible if they are kept too swampy or if it came already infected, but your close ups seem to show healthy growing buds coming up right at the bottom.

And if this one just didn't happen to be as mature as the others when you bought it, could be it's just struggling a bit to get settled. I bought a pistachio hydrangea early this spring and it's only just getting settled now. But the other, larger ones I bought over the summer are flourishing. Little pistachio was just taken from his mom too early and needed some extra care.

Looking at this variety online....it's soooooo pretty! It's too tender for my zone 5a in Canada, though. Lucky you that you can grow it!
